blocks.prompt: It's 8:30. Which word completes the answer?
blocks.explanationEnglish: 'Halb neun' counts forward to the next hour — half [to] nine is 8:30.

concept.title: Halb N = halbe Stunde vor N
concept.rule: German tells time by counting TO the next hour. 'Halb neun' is 8:30, 'halb sechs' is 5:30. Never translate 'half past' literally.

blocks.explanationEnglish: 'um' introduces clock times, and the accusative only ever changes masculine articles.

concept.title: Temporalpräpositionen
concept.rule: Clock time → 'um' (um acht Uhr). Day → 'am' (am Montag). Month/year → 'im' (im Mai). Fixed phrases: 'am Morgen', 'am Abend'.
concept.exampleGerman: Um acht Uhr gehe ich zur Arbeit.
concept.exampleEnglish: At eight o'clock I go to work.

blocks.prompt: Choose the correct article for ordering a coffee.
blocks.explanationEnglish: 'der Kaffee' is masculine and becomes the direct object of 'möchten', so it shifts to the accusative 'einen'.

concept.title: Akkusativ: nur Maskulinum ändert sich
concept.rule: In the accusative only masculine nouns change: der → den, ein → einen, kein → keinen. Feminine, neuter and plural stay as they are.
concept.exampleGerman: Ich möchte einen Kuchen. — Ich möchte eine Milch.
concept.exampleEnglish: I'd like a cake. — I'd like a milk.

blocks.explanationEnglish: Unit first, then 'und', then the decade — the reverse of English.

concept.title: Zahlen 21–99: Einers zuerst
concept.rule: For 21–99 German reverses the order: unit + und + decade. 'Einundzwanzig' = one-and-twenty. Above 99 normal order returns: 'hundertzwanzig'.

blocks.prompt: How do you say the cents?
blocks.explanationEnglish: Cents are stated as the full number: 50 cents is 'fünfzig'.

concept.title: Preise aussprechen
concept.rule: German quotes prices as euros then cents in full numbers: 7,50 → 'sieben Euro fünfzig'. The decimal comma reads as a gap, not 'point'.
